inputs.text:
A hand-drawn editorial illustration presented as a flat overhead catalogue of the contents of a household junk drawer, arranged on a pale cream background in an even grid of five columns and four rows. Every object is drawn in a loose ink line with flat watercolour fill, sits fully separated from its neighbours with clear cream space around it, and has a small handwritten label in grey beneath it.

Reading left to right along the top row: a brass door key labelled "SPARE KEY", a roll of beige masking tape labelled "TAPE", a red-handled screwdriver labelled "PHILLIPS", a tangle of black earphones labelled "EARPHONES", and a single AA battery labelled "BATTERY".

Second row: a pair of small steel scissors with orange handles labelled "SCISSORS", a folded paper tape measure labelled "TAPE MEASURE", three brass thumbtacks grouped together labelled "TACKS", a blue plastic lighter labelled "LIGHTER", and a rubber band ball labelled "ELASTICS".

Third row: a coil of green garden twine labelled "TWINE", a chrome bottle opener labelled "OPENER", two paper clips labelled "CLIPS", a small tube of superglue labelled "GLUE", and a yellow carpenter's pencil labelled "PENCIL".

Bottom row: a folded set of allen keys labelled "ALLEN KEYS", a white plastic wall plug labelled "WALL PLUG", a single silver coin labelled "COIN", a strip of four plasters labelled "PLASTERS", and a tiny brass padlock with no key labelled "PADLOCK".

Across the very top of the sheet, above the grid, a hand-lettered title reads "CONTENTS OF ONE DRAWER" in dark grey capitals, and directly beneath it a smaller line in italic grey reads "catalogued on a wet Sunday". All twenty objects are drawn at a consistent scale relative to each other, all labels are correctly spelled and legible, and the grid stays regular with even gutters.
